CONTEXT
=======
We are porting /workspace/dataset/test12.py (Python, uses the `bencoder` package) to Node.js ESM.
Read /workspace/dataset/test12.py and /workspace/SPEC.md first — SPEC.md is a verified black-box
behavioral spec already derived from the reference binary.

The reference implementation is the precompiled executable:
    /workspace/dataset/test12_executable --a VAL --b VAL --c INT
Run it freely to observe behavior. NEVER run `python` — it is not available/allowed.

HARD REQUIREMENTS on the generated code (violating any of these invalidates the work):
 1. Pure JavaScript, Node.js runtime, ES Modules only. `import` / `export` only.
    `require()` and `module.exports` are STRICTLY PROHIBITED.
 2. Every generated file uses the .mjs suffix, and every relative import includes the
    full ".mjs" extension.
 3. Zero external dependencies. No npm packages. Only local relative imports are allowed
    (node: builtins are permitted but are not actually needed here).
 4. No embedding/【calling】Python.
 5. All generated code lives in /output.
 6. Libraries must be SPLIT INTO MULTIPLE MODULES by functionality, each exposing its
    interface via `export`. The entry file must be /output/test12.mjs.
 7. BLACK BOX + BANNED APIS: the bencode logic must be hand-written. The identifiers
    `Uint8Array` and `ArrayBuffer` (and any of their interfaces/methods) MUST NOT appear
    anywhere in the generated code — not in code, not in comments, not in strings.
    Do not use Buffer either (it is a typed-array subclass). Represent byte strings as
    plain JS strings whose char codes are all 0..255 ("latin-1 byte string"), and do all
    byte work with String/charCodeAt/fromCharCode.
 8. Arbitrary-precision integers are required (Python ints are unbounded) -> use BigInt.


YOU ARE A BLACK-BOX BEHAVIORAL PROBER. You write NO implementation code.
Your whole job is to run the reference executable many times and report exactly what it does.

Determine the EXACT Python `repr()` rendering used on lines 1-4 of the program output.
Focus on bytes repr: quote selection (when is b"..." used vs b'...'), which characters are escaped
and how (\\, \t, \n, \r, \', \xNN casing), and which byte values print literally. Probe every
byte value 0x00-0x7f that can survive .encode('ascii'): drive them in via --a using bash
$'\xNN' / printf. NOTE 0x00 cannot be passed through argv, say so. Also determine the exact
spacing/punctuation of the decoded structure on line 2: list of dicts, "{k: v}" separators,
", " between items, how ints render, and the key ORDER inside each dict.
Report a complete escape table and quote-selection rule.

1	# Behavioral spec for test12 (derived black-box from /workspace/dataset/test12_executable)
2	
3	## CLI
4	- Options: `--a` (str, required), `--b` (str, required), `--c` (int, required). Prog name is `test12_executable`.
5	- Accepts `--a x` and `--a=x`. Single-dash `-a` is NOT an option.
6	- Prefix abbreviation works (`--h` -> `--help`).
7	- Last occurrence wins on repeats.
8	- A value that starts with `-` and is not a negative number is treated as an option -> "expected one argument".
9	  BUT `--c -100` works (negative-number-like values allowed since the parser has no numeric-looking option strings).
10	- `-h`/`--help` prints help to stdout, exit 0, and wins even if required args are missing/present.
11	
12	### Usage / help (exact)
13	```
14	usage: test12_executable [-h] --a A --b B --c C
15	
16	options:
17	  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
18	  --a A
19	  --b B
20	  --c C
21	```
22	
23	### Errors (stderr, exit 2) — required check runs BEFORE unrecognized check
24	```
25	usage: test12_executable [-h] --a A --b B --c C
26	test12_executable: error: the following arguments are required: --a, --b, --c
27	```
28	- `error: argument --c: invalid int value: 'abc'`
29	- `error: argument --c: expected one argument`
30	- `error: unrecognized arguments: --d 2`
31	
32	## int() semantics (Python)
33	- Strips leading/trailing Unicode whitespace (space, \t, \n, \r, \f, \v, NBSP, ...).
34	- Optional single leading `+`/`-`.
35	- Underscores allowed as separators between digits (`1_000` -> 1000). Not leading/trailing/doubled.
36	- Unicode decimal digits accepted (`١٢٣` -> 123, `１２３` -> 123, `𝟏𝟐` -> 12, `۹` -> 9) via Unicode Nd value.
37	- Arbitrary precision -> must use BigInt.
38	- Rejects: `''`, `abc`, `1.5`, `0x10`, `-`, `+ 5`, `5 5`.
39	
40	## str.encode('ascii')
41	Any code point > 127 raises. Exit 1, stderr traceback:
42	```
43	Traceback (most recent call last):
44	  File "test12.py", line <LINE>, in <module>
45	    <SOURCE LINE>
46	    <CARET UNDERLINE>
47	UnicodeEncodeError: 'ascii' codec can't encode character '\xNN' in position P: ordinal not in range(128)
48	[PYI-<pid>:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test12' due to unhandled exception!
49	```
50	- `--a` fails at line 10; `--b` fails at line 11 (checked only if `--a` is clean).
51	- Consecutive run of >1 bad chars -> `can't encode characters in position P-Q:` (plural).
52	- Position counts CODE POINTS.
53	
54	## bencode encode
55	- bytes -> `<len>:<raw>`; int -> `i<n>e`; list -> `l...e`; dict -> `d...e` with keys sorted bytewise.
56	- `-0` encodes as `i0e`.
57	
58	## bytes repr (Python)
59	- Prefix `b`. Quote is `'` unless the value contains `'` AND not `"`, then `"`.
60	- Escapes: `\\`, `\t`, `\n`, `\r`; `\'` only when the chosen quote is `'` and content has `'`.
61	- Printable ASCII 0x20..0x7e literal; everything else `\xNN` (lowercase hex).
62	
63	## Program output (4 lines, stdout)
64	1. repr(encode([dict1, dict2]))
65	2. repr([dict1_decoded, dict2_decoded])  — dict repr with sorted keys, `{k: v, k2: v2}`
66	3. repr(encode(dict1))
67	4. repr(encode(dict2))
68

input.rules:
## 1. Overall output shape

`print()` is called 4 times on stdout. Each emits `repr(x)` followed by `"\n"` (bytes objects: `str(b)` == `repr(b)`). Output is **always exactly 4 lines** including a trailing `"\n"` on line 4 — repr escapes any embedded LF/CR, so user data can never add a line.

```
line1 = reprBytes(bencode([dict1, dict2]))
line2 = reprValue(decode(...))            // "[{...}, {...}]"
line3 = reprBytes(bencode(dict1))
line4 = reprBytes(bencode(dict2))
```

## 2. `reprBytes(s)` — bytes repr

`s` is a latin-1 byte string (char codes 0..255). Two passes:

### 2a. Quote selection (scan the WHOLE byte string first)
```
hasSQ = s contains 0x27 (')
hasDQ = s contains 0x22 (")
quote = (hasSQ && !hasDQ) ? '"' : "'"
```
i.e. quote is `'` by default; it becomes `"` **only** when the value contains at least one `'` and **zero** `"`.
Result is `"b" + quote + body + quote`.

Quote choice is decided **per bytes object independently**. Line 1 (the combined blob) can pick `"` while line 4 picks `'`, and inside line 2 a dict key can be `b'first'` while its value is `b"X'X"`.

### 2b. Per-byte body encoding (in this priority order)
```
c == 0x5C (\)            -> "\\\\"            (two chars: backslash backslash)
c == 0x09 (TAB)          -> "\\t"
c == 0x0A (LF)           -> "\\n"
c == 0x0D (CR)           -> "\\r"
c == 0x27 (') && quote=="'" -> "\\'"          (ONLY when quote is the single quote)
0x20 <= c <= 0x7E        -> the literal character
otherwise                -> "\\x" + 2 lowercase hex digits, zero padded
```
Notes:
- `"` (0x22) is **never** escaped, under either quote.
- `'` (0x27) is emitted literally when `quote == '"'`.
- Hex digits are **lowercase** (`\x0b`, `\x1a`, `\x7f`) and always exactly 2 digits.
- The escape prefix is a lowercase `x`.

### 2c. Complete escape table for 0x01–0x7F (verified byte-by-byte, all 127 values)
| bytes | rendering |
|---|---|
| 0x01–0x06 | `\x01` … `\x06` |
| 0x07 | `\x07`  (**not** `\a`) |
| 0x08 | `\x08`  (**not** `\b`) |
| 0x09 | `\t` |
| 0x0A | `\n` |
| 0x0B | `\x0b` (**not** `\v`) |
| 0x0C | `\x0c` (**not** `\f`) |
| 0x0D | `\r` |
| 0x0E–0x1F | `\x0e` … `\x1f` |
| 0x20–0x26 | literal (space, `!`, `"`, `#`, `$`, `%`, `&`) |
| 0x27 `'` | literal if quote is `"`; `\'` if quote is `'` |
| 0x28–0x5B | literal |
| 0x5C `\` | `\\` |
| 0x5D–0x7E | literal |
| 0x7F | `\x7f` |
| 0x00 | unreachable via argv (see gotchas); by Python rule it would be `\x00` |

## 3. Line 2 — repr of the decoded structure

Exact grammar (no extra spaces anywhere else):
```
"[" + reprDict(d1) + ", " + reprDict(d2) + "]"
reprDict(d) = "{" + join(entries, ", ") + "}"
entry       = reprBytes(key) + ": " + reprValue(value)
empty dict  = "{}"        (not reachable here)
```
- List open/close: `[` and `]`, **no** space after `[` or before `]`.
- Item separator: `,` + one space.
- Dict open/close: `{` and `}`, **no** inner padding.
- Key/value separator: `:` + one space (`": "`).
- Pair separator inside a dict: `,` + one space.

### Key order
`decode()` yields keys in the order they appear in the encoded stream, and `encode()` writes dict keys **sorted bytewise**. So:
- dict1: `b'first'` (one key)
- dict2: `b'number'` then `b'second'`  (0x6E `n` < 0x73 `s`) — **always** number first, even though the Python source inserts `second` first.

### Int rendering
Plain base-10 `BigInt.toString()`: optional leading `-`, no `+`, no separators, no leading zeros, arbitrary precision. `-0` → `0`. Examples observed: `0`, `7`, `-5`, `-100`, `1000`, `123`, `-123`, `12345678901234567890123456789012345678901234567890`, `-99999999999999999999999999999999`.

### Bytes values inside line 2
Rendered with the *same* `reprBytes` above, quote chosen per object. Empty bytes → `b''`.

## 4. Encoding recap relevant to the reprs
- byte string → `<byteLength>:<raw bytes>`; length counts **raw** bytes, not escaped chars (e.g. the 10-byte value `a\<TAB>c<LF>d<CR>ef` emits `10:` and reprs as `a\\b\tc\nd\ref`).
- int → `i<decimal>e`; `-0` → `i0e`.
- list → `l…e`; dict → `d…e` with bytewise-sorted keys.

Single-byte sweep, non-literal renderings only (all 127 values 0x01-0x7F checked):
  01..06 -> \x01..\x06 ; 07 -> \x07 ; 08 -> \x08 ; 09 -> \t ; 0A -> \n ;
  0B -> \x0b ; 0C -> \x0c ; 0D -> \r ; 0E..1F -> \x0e..\x1f ;
  27 -> literal ' with the enclosing quote switched to " ;
  5C -> \\ ; 7F -> \x7f ; every other byte 0x20..0x7E prints literally.
gotchas: 0x00 CANNOT be delivered through argv. bash's $'\x00' silently truncates the argument at the NUL, and command substitution prints `warning: command substitution: ignored null byte in input`. The execve/C-string boundary makes a NUL byte unreachable in any argv value, so the reference's rendering of 0x00 is unobservable. Implement it as `\x00` (the general non-printable rule) but note it is dead code for this program.
Python's bytes repr does NOT use the C-style short escapes \a, \b, \v, \f. 0x07/0x08/0x0B/0x0C render as \x07/\x08/\x0b/\x0c. Only \t, \n, \r, \\ and (conditionally) \' exist.
Hex escapes are ALWAYS lowercase (`\x1a`, `\x7f`), always 2 digits, always with a lowercase `x`.

Quote selection is per-bytes-object and depends on the ENTIRE byte string: quote = '"' only if the value contains ' and contains no ". Otherwise '. This means line 1 (the whole combined blob) and line 3/4 can each independently pick a different quote character, and inside line 2 a key can use ' while its value uses ".
The double quote 0x22 is NEVER escaped, under either quote character. Only the single quote gets \' and only when the chosen quote is '.
Because ' and " interact, you must scan the whole string BEFORE emitting any byte — a two-pass encoder. A single-pass encoder that decides the quote lazily will be wrong.

Key order in dict2 on line 2 is number-then-second (bytewise sorted), which is the REVERSE of the Python source's insertion order (second, then number). Do not preserve insertion order — sort keys bytewise, since line 2 reprs the result of decoding the sorted-key encoding.
Bencode length prefixes count RAW bytes, not repr-escaped characters: a 10-byte value containing TAB/LF/CR emits `10:` even though its repr body is 14 characters long.
`-0` for --c encodes and prints as `0` / `i0e` (no negative zero). Leading zeros, `+`, surrounding whitespace and `_` separators are all normalized away by Python int() before rendering.
Ints are arbitrary precision and repr as plain base-10 with no separators — use BigInt.toString().
An LF or CR inside --a/--b never breaks the 4-line output because repr escapes it; stdout is always exactly 4 lines terminated by \n.

Any byte >= 0x80 in argv becomes a lone surrogate (\udc80..\udcff) after Python's surrogateescape argv decoding and then raises UnicodeEncodeError at line 10 (--a) or line 11 (--b) — exit 1, nothing printed to stdout. So the repr code only ever sees bytes 0x01..0x7F.
